quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Encourage other friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: You can prevent drunk driving by arranging other transportation, keeping them busy to slow their drinking, finding excuses to delay them until they are sober, and asking other friends to help stop them.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should generally ride:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps the group close together while giving each rider enough space around them. Use single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The near side of the lane is safer.
You will feel a stronger wind blast on the far side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may tempt the driver to re-enter your lane before they have enough room to do so safely.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips (less than five miles) at slow speeds (less than 30 mph).

questions.question: Helmeted riders are ________ more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets.
questions.explanation: At any speed, wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash than not wearing one.

questions.question: During the day, your headlight should:

options.text: Switch between high and low beam.

questions.explanation: Using your high beam during the day helps other drivers see you. Use high beam whenever you are not riding behind or meeting other vehicles.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must have all of these features, except:

options.text: Be too tight for sunglasses or eyeglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be too tight for sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be scratch-free, resistant to breaking, allow clear views to the sides, fasten securely, let air flow to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: The oily strip in the center of a lane:

options.text: Is usually safe for motorcyclists unless the road is wet.
Should always be avoided since other parts of the lane are safer.
Improves traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. On dry roads, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles. Since the oily strip is usually only about two feet wide, you can ride to one side of it and still stay in the lane's center area.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Use arms to hold their body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Keep your arms slightly bent on the handgrips. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see the road through vehicles in front of you.
When the weather is pleasant and clear.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when you need more time to stop. This includes heavy traffic, bad weather, wet roads, nighttime, and when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Making eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you. Keep a safe space around you to avoid danger. Never assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: Why should you not change gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Other drivers may not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface makes shifting gears harder.

questions.explanation: Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle could stall while you are on the tracks.

questions.question: Motorcycles appear to be traveling faster than they actually are because of their:
questions.explanation: Because motorcycles are small, they may appear to be going faster than they actually are.

questions.question: How does a load in a sidecar affect stopping distance?

options.text: It does not affect stopping distance.
It has the same effect as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Adding weight to a motorcycle increases its inertia and makes it take longer to stop. Start slowing down earlier when carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are about to slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are about to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before you slow down suddenly. A driver following too closely may not see hazards ahead. The warning gives them time to react.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should always be avoided?

options.text: The left part of the lane.
The center part of the lane.
The right part of the lane.
No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best or always bad. Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How should you look when riding through a turn?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol was consumed.
How often a person drinks alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol.
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also matter. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance in ideal conditions?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance whenever conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop far behind the vehicle, then slowly move up.
Stop quickly right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both are stopped. The vehicle could back up without warning. You also need space to move if another vehicle hits you from behind.

questions.question: An integrated braking system:

options.text: Uses some rear braking when you apply the front brake.
Uses some front braking when you apply the rear brake.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear brakes at the same time.
Remembers how hard you brake and learns your style.

questions.correctAnswerText: Uses some front braking when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system connects the brakes together. When you use the rear brake, it automatically applies some front braking too. Read your motorcycle's owner's manual to learn more about your specific braking system.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you from behind, you should:

options.text: Move to the center of the lane.
Move to the left side of the lane.
Move to the right side of the lane.
Stay in whatever lane position you are using.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When another vehicle passes you, ride in the center of your lane. Staying close to the passing vehicle increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front of the group, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch over them without making the new rider lead the entire group.

questions.question: How can you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve toward the side with fewer hazards.
Try to speed up while braking.

questions.explanation: To regain control when the rear wheel locks, release the brake immediately. However, if you lock the rear brake on a dry road, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: At minimum, how often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid?
questions.explanation: Check your hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week. Regular pre-ride checks help keep your motorcycle safe.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam (unless following another car), use other vehicles' headlights to see, and wear reflective gear. Change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen better, and stay safe.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done to avoid hazards on slippery roads.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a fast move that needs good traction to work safely. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on wet or slippery surfaces.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve, not both.
Only brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions one after the other, not at the same time. Braking while swerving at the same time can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: If the road is wet, you should avoid:

options.text: The left side of a lane.
The right side of the lane.

questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks collects in the center of lanes. This area usually has enough grip for motorcycles, except when wet. The oily strip is usually narrow, so you can ride beside it and still stay in the center area of the lane.
